chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Chick Corea's Suite for a Hot Band
summary: Corea wrote an 18-20 minute three-movement piece; the first movement should sound like 'Stravinsky meets Sousa'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. No, the album that -- your latest album, which is the object of a lot of enthusiasm, you look upon that as maybe a high spot in your long career.
It's one of the high spots, yes.
Yeah. You want to talk a little bit about that album, since it's pretty unusual.
Well, in the first place, it's a couple of different kinds of material.

And Chick Corea particularly, writing a piece, a very serious piece by your standards and mine, a piece that runs about 18 to 20 minutes, and it's in three complete movements, three parts. And I think it's a complete work of art for this particular age we're living in.
Uh-huh. This "Suite for a Hot Band," by Chick Corea, you're talking about.

Right. And his description of just the first movement when we were first rehearsing it, many months ago, that the first movement should sound like Stravinsky meets Sousa. And I think this is very descriptive of what he wrote.
And yet, the second movement is another mood com-
pletely. It's a blues feeling and a blues aspect, and the last movement is back into what we think of as typical Corea Latin, of some form or variety.
